questions.question: A feature has mean 10 and standard deviation 5. After standardization, what value represents x=15?
For min-max scaling to [0,1], what is the scaled value of x=7 when the observed minimum is 2 and maximum is 12?
Why must target-encoding statistics be computed separately inside each training fold?
options: Using validation targets would leak the answer into the feature
Target encoding only works for numeric labels
Fold-specific statistics make categories alphabetically ordered
Validation rows cannot contain categorical values
questions.explanation: The category mean must be learned without seeing held-out targets; otherwise the validation score is optimistic.

questions.question: What is the main reason TF-IDF downweights a word that appears in nearly every document?
options: It removes every word that appears twice
Its inverse-document-frequency factor is small, so it carries little document-specific information
It replaces word order with random numbers
It gives common words the largest possible weight
questions.explanation: A word found in many documents has low inverse document frequency and is less useful for distinguishing documents.

questions.question: A color column contains red, green, and blue with no natural order. Which encoding avoids inventing a numeric ranking?
options: The mean of the three color names
Drop every row containing a color
questions.explanation: One-hot columns represent membership without implying that blue is greater than green or red.

questions.question: You want to remove an almost-constant numeric feature before fitting a model. Which filter is directly suited to that goal?
options: A target mean computed using the test labels
A random permutation of the feature names
A one-hot encoder applied to the response
A variance threshold computed on the training data
questions.explanation: Variance thresholding removes features with little variation. The threshold is fitted on training data to avoid using held-out information.
